## Introduction
This project uses a retrospective cohort of patients who underwent epilepsy surgery. The dataset was simulated using plausible relationships between variables for the purposes of practicing reproducible research workflows with Git, GitHub, Python, and Quarto. It contains no real patient information.

The main analysis examines whether agreement among presurgical evaluation modalities is associated with one-year Engel outcome.

The following report walks through the steps of the analysis, from data inspection to figure generation and statistical analysis.

## Initial data inspection
The raw dataset was deliberately generated with a small number of plausible errors in a retrospective medical records analysis, such as missing fields, inconsistencies in capitalization, or improbable values. The inspection script identifies the affected patient IDs for the researcher to decide how to fix the issue.

## Data cleaning
The cleaning script preserves the raw CSV and creates a separate cleaned dataset. It removes exact duplicate rows, standardizes the inconsistent localization label, replaces implausible onset ages and seizure frequencies with missing values, and recalculates epilepsy duration from the available ages.

Later analyses should utilize the cleaned data.
```{python}
#| label: clean-data
#| echo: true
%run scripts/data_cleaning.py
```
After cleaning, the dataset contains `{python} len(clean_data)` unique patient records.

The dataset contains records from adult and pediatric epilepsy cases. The average age at surgery was 33.9 ± 19.4 years. With an average presurgical epilepsy duration (from diagnosis to surgery) of 19 ± 14.1 years. The most common localization was temporal (57.7%), followed by frontal (20.0%).The most common surgery type was a tie between temporal resection and lesionectomy (32.7% and 32.7% respectively). 

## Presurgical evaluation
 MRI and scalp EEG were performed for nearly all patients, while PET, MEG, and intracranial EEG were used more selectively.

## Multimodal concordance and surgical outcome
The number of concordant presurgical modalities was compared with the ordered Engel outcome using Spearman rank correlation. Lower Engel classes represent better one-year surgical outcomes. 
```{python}
#| label: fig-concordance-outcome
#| fig-cap: "One-year Engel outcome by the number of concordant presurgical modalities."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| echo: false
from scripts.make_figures import plot_concordance_by_outcome
concord_fig = plot_concordance_by_outcome()
```
The simulated cohort showed a small association between greater multimodal concordance and better surgical outcome.
